name: Two denial rule
plain: After two denials, Android stops showing the permission dialog.
meaning: Limits repeated prompts. iOS shows a permission prompt only once; later changes must be made in Settings.

android.prompt_ui: Dialog shows at most twice per permission
android.persistence: Remains denied until user changes it
android.store_policy: Play: apps must handle denial gracefully
android.note: USER_SET after one denial; USER_FIXED after two.

ios.note: App can send the user to Settings via a deep link.

limits.headline: Can ask for a permission only twice on Android, and once on iPhone
limits.user_action: You tap Don't allow on a permission dialog
can: Ask again after one denial on Android
Send you to Settings with a link to change it
Explain why it needs the permission before asking again
cannot: Show the Android dialog after two denials
Show the iPhone prompt again after you answer
Change the permission for you; you do that in Settings
limits.reach_label: One or two asks, then Settings
limits.differs: Android shows the dialog at most twice; iPhone shows it once.

story.what_it_is: After you say no twice, Android stops showing the permission prompt for that app.
story.for_you: If you deny a permission twice, the app cannot ask again. You have to change it yourself in Settings. This stops an app from nagging you into saying yes.
story.for_makers: Apps must explain why they need a permission before asking, since they only get two tries. Good apps show a simple screen first. Bad ones may send you to Settings with a plea.

use_cases.example: A game asks for location, you say no twice, and it works without it or shows a settings link.
A social app asks for contacts and has to live without it after two denials.
A maps app shows a screen explaining why location helps before the prompt.
A store app asks for the camera and sends you to Settings if you refuse twice.
A fitness app asks for body sensors and explains its use.
A researcher tests how an app behaves when permissions are blocked.
A developer builds a pre prompt screen to win consent.

story.android_note: Android marks a permission as user set after one denial, and fixed after two.
story.ios_note: iPhone shows a permission prompt only once. After that, changes must be made in Settings, and an app can link to Settings.
